evidence: All 43 Functional (weight sum 58.5), 5 Polish, 5 Visual criteria and both gates were walked pairwise. Most ownership boundaries are explicit and sound: hro_arrive_bottom defers multi-card arrival to hro_bulk_move; hro_interview_full defers bulk overfill to hro_bulk_places and undo overfill to hro_undo_full; hro_activity vs hro_activity_refusals (functional prompt.md:19 assigns refused-action lines only to the latter); hro_drafts defers send-clearing to hro_msg_compose; hro_pol_live_thread owns draft/focus while scrolled-up place is Functional; hro_pol_failed_send defers note drafts to hro_pol_session_resume; hro_candidate_view defers privacy to hro_candidate_private and reply to hro_msg_exchange; hro_candidate_linked 'alone owns that link'. No pair demands incompatible products (candidate board/activity reads 'refused or answered with only own data' is lenient vs rules 7 but compatible; hro_anonymous 401 and hro_candidate_private 404 match hireops_rules.md section 1). Visual Likert rows split type/color/layout/hierarchy/consistency with no shared observable beyond normal craft overlap. DEFECT: one observation is graded by two scored rows. Functional prompt.md:35 step (12) performs a SINGLE undo of A2's move after BOTH a note was added to A2 and Mei re-ordered a different card Y. That one undo outcome is the positive leg of hro_undo_restores (judge.toml:236 'undo of A2's move goes ahead after a note was added to A2 and puts A2 back in Applied ... Fails if ... the note blocks the undo', weight 2) and is also the required same-kind control of hro_undo_conflict (judge.toml:245 'when another person changes only a different card of the job, Rafael's undo goes ahead ... Fails if ... the undo after an unrelated change is refused', weight 2). If that undo is refused, both rows fail, and the judge cannot tell from the observation whether the note or the unrelated re-order caused it. The prompt's tie-break 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' (functional prompt.md:23) does not name an owner and conflicts with each row's own 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold', so the result depends on judge choice. Notes (not counted as the Fail): (a) many rows share a precondition by design as positive controls (live arrival within 15 s gates hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_*, hro_seen and polish hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread which say 'this row is 0' without arrival; candidate sign-in gates hro_candidate_no_staff/private/view) - REVIEW_POLICY 'a negative needs a successful control' supports this; it is cascade/discrimination (rows 30/40) rather than double-grading of one promise. (b) hro_interview_full ('that card stays where it was', judge.toml:110) and hro_refused_put_back ('card is shown in its real stage and place', judge.toml:137) observe the same attempt; full is server refusal, put_back is the on-page rollback, but an optimistic UI that never rolls back may be read as 'accepted through the UI' and lose both - a P3 wording risk. Not exercised: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope), so actual judge deduction behaviour is unmeasured.
counterexample: A conforming-elsewhere app that invalidates a pending undo whenever any card in the same stage is renumbered (or whenever a note bumps the card version) refuses the step-(12) A2 undo. That single defect fails hro_undo_restores (A2 leg) and hro_undo_conflict (control leg): 4.0/58.5 of Functional (~6.8%, ~4.1% of total reward) for one behaviour, whereas each promise was meant to be worth 2.0. Conversely a judge applying 'never deduct twice' must arbitrarily pass one of the two rows although its stated condition did not hold.
suggested_fix: Split step (12) into two undo events - A2 move + note + undo (owned by hro_undo_restores) and a separate move + another person's change to a different card + undo (control of hro_undo_conflict) - or name the single owner of a refused A2 undo in both criterion texts.
